picked.t: 베트남, ‘7월 27일 상이군인·열사의 날’ 공휴일 지정 추진…통과 시 내년부터 시행
picked.body: 지난달 호치민시에서 1968년 베트남전 당시 구정 대공세 당시 발굴된 전몰자 유해를 레 민 흥 베트남 총리(앞줄 오른쪽) 등 베트남 지도부가 운구 중인 모습.  (사진=베트남정부포털) 베트남 정부가 법개정을 통해 매년 7월 27일을 상이군인·순국열사의 날로 지정, 공휴일을 추가하는 방안을 추진하고 있다. 이번 노동법 개정안에는 11월 24일 베트남 문화의 날 역시 공휴일로 담겨 있어, 개정안이 통과되면 베트남의 연간 공휴일은 현재 11일에서  13일로 늘어날 전망이다. 9일 오전 베트남 국회는 노동법과 기록보존법, 양성평등법, 적십자활동법, 고용법의 일부개정·보완안을 심의했다. 이날 법안 설명에서 응우옌 띠엔 하이(Nguyen Tien Hai) 베트남 내무부 장관은 “노동법 개정안에 매년 7월 27일을 상이군인·열사의 날로 지정, 내년부터 법정공휴일로 시행하자는 제안을 받아들였다”고 설명했다. 그는 이어 “이번 공휴일 추가안은 국가유공자와 혁명유공자를 기리고, 근로자들로 하여금 보은하는 활동에 참여하고 민족의 아름다운 전통을 이어가도록 하려는 취지”라고 덧붙였다. 상이군인·열사의 날 외에도 개정안에는 정치국 결의안 제80호를 법제화하기 위해 11월 24일 베트남 문화의 날을 올해부터 법정공휴일로 지정한다는 내용이 담겼다. 현재 베트남의 공휴일은 연간 11일로, 여기에는 △신정 1일 △뗏(Tet 설) 5일 △훙왕기일(음력 3월 10일) 1일 △통일절(남부해방기념일, 4월 30일) 1일 △노동절(5월 1일) 1일 △국경절(9월 2일) 2일 등이 포함된다. 여기에 개정안을 통해 상이군인·열사의 날(2027년 시행)과 베트남 문화의 날(11월 24일)이 추가되면 내년부터 연간 공휴일은 13일로 늘어난다. 앞서 베트남 정부는 지난 2019년 노동법 개정 당시에도 7월 27일을 공휴일로 지정하는 방안을 추진한 바 있다. 정부는 당시 “상이군인·열사의 날은 문화적 상징이 됐고 민족의 보은 전통을 보여준다”며 “해외 여러 국가에서도 유사한 성격의 날을 공휴일로 지정하고 있어 국제적 관행과도 일치한다”고 설명했다. 그러나 해당 방안은 국회 문턱을 넘지 못했는데, 일부 의원들은 열사와 유공자에 대한 보은 활동이 정기적으로 이뤄지고 있는 점, 전몰자 유가족들의 슬픔을 되살리고 장기화할 수 있다는 점 등을 이유로 반대 의사를 피력했다.

picked.t: Vietnam targets at least 10% GDP growth and $6,100 per capita GDP in 2027
picked.body: The legislature passed a resolution on the country's 2027 socio-economic development plan on Saturday, with more than 93.4% of lawmakers voting in favor. Under the resolution, Vietnam aims to achieve economic growth of at least 10% next year while keeping inflation at around 4.5%. The resolution calls on the government to continue prioritizing growth while maintaining macroeconomic stability, controlling inflation and ensuring major economic balances. The government is also tasked with making breakthroughs in mobilizing and efficiently allocating resources for development. Measures include increasing state budget revenue, cutting expenditure, particularly recurrent spending, issuing various types of bonds and securing official development assistance (ODA) loans. It must also promptly implement policies to raise foreign ownership limits in industries and sectors that do not affect national security. The National Assembly urged the government to manage interest and exchange rates in line with domestic and international conditions, lower lending rates and direct credit toward production, business activities and priority sectors. The government is also expected to introduce effective measures to address trade deficit, develop a healthy and sustainable real estate market, and resolve long-standing stalled projects. To ensure energy security, the resolution requires the government to guarantee sufficient supplies of electricity and petroleum products under all circumstances. On infrastructure, the government is tasked with completing the expressway network in line with approved plans, particularly the eastern and western sections of the North-South Expressway and East-West transport corridors. It must also accelerate major national railway projects, including the Lao Cai-Hanoi-Hai Phong railway, the North-South high-speed railway, international rail connections and urban railway networks. The resolution calls for faster progress on two major airport projects: Long Thanh International Airport in Dong Nai, about 40 kilometers east of Ho Chi Minh City, and Gia Binh International Airport in Bac Ninh Province, 40 km east of central Hanoi. Long Thanh is being developed to ease pressure on HCMC's Tan Son Nhat International Airport and eventually handle 100 million passengers annually. Gia Binh is planned as a major aviation gateway for northern Vietnam, serving passenger and cargo transport, international transit and aircraft maintenance. In the energy sector, the National Assembly requires the government to develop a national energy reserve strategy and accelerate planned power generation, transmission grid and solar power projects. It also urged authorities to firmly address the trend of localities pursuing airport, seaport, data center and free trade zone investments without proper planning, warning against wasteful spending.

picked.t: Steak, pizza, and French food: 8 European restaurants to try in Hanoi
picked.body: Chien Beo Steak After remaining closed for nearly a decade, Chien Beo Steak reopened in mid-2025. It had once been a popular destination for generations of Hanoian families. Its standout dishes include cheese-wrapped beef rolls and steak, made in a style adapted to Vietnamese palates. The restaurant's seating area is now cleaner and more spacious than before. Tables can be hard to book since they are often full. Chien Beo only serves dinner and is closed on Mondays. Address: 69 Hoang Nhu Tiep Street, Long Bien Ward. Prices start at VND250,000 ($9.60) per person. Pizza 4P's chain Pizza 4P's, a Japanese Italian pizza chain, offers a range of pizzas with thin crusts alongside pasta, salads, and desserts. It is good for families with children and groups of friends. Its spaces are dotted with greenery, and diners can watch the chefs at work. Address: Bao Khanh Street, Trang Tien Street, Au Co Street, Lotte Center, and Hanoi Center. Prices start at VND300,000 ($11.50) per person. La Bodega La Bodega spreads across a space of 2,500 square meters at a location quite far from the city center. The menu features Italian and European staples like pizza, pasta, and grilled meats. A standout dish to try is the Picanha BBQ, a top sirloin cap beef cut. The restaurant seats 200 guests and often hosts gatherings of friends, family parties, and small events. Address: Alley 56/139 Thach Cau, Long Bien Ward. Prices start at VND300,000 per person. Caffè Italia (Casa Italia) Set in Hanoi's Italian Cultural Center (Casa Italia), the restaurant features a spacious Mediterranean garden perfect for outdoor dining and wine. The menu includes Italian classics like pizza, pasta, and gelato. The restaurant also has a board on which it lists dishes outside the regular menu, which changes frequently. Address: 18 Le Phung Hieu Street, Hoan Kiem Ward. Prices range from VND300,000 to VND500,000 per person. Mediterraneo Mediterraneo stands out for its setting. Some tables offer a view of St. Joseph's Cathedral. It is a good choice for people looking to try Italian cuisine beyond just pizza and pasta. Tripadvisor recommends Mediterraneo among Italian restaurants to try in Hanoi, and it won a Travelers' Choice award in 2025. Address: 23 Nha Tho Street, Hoan Kiem Ward. Prices range from VND500,000 to VND700,000 per person, not including alcoholic drinks. Cugini Cugini positions itself as a bistro focused on modern Italian cuisine. Its appeal lies in the balance it strikes between food quality and atmosphere. The restaurant has an outdoor seating area and a second floor. Cugini is more affordable than Hanoi's high-end Italian restaurants, and comes recommended by Tripadvisor. Address: 67 To Ngoc Van Street, Tay Ho Ward. Prices start at around VND400,000 per person, not including alcoholic drinks. Colette French Bistro & Wine Bar Colette is compact and in French bistro style. The menu centers on French dishes such as tuna tartare, beef braised in wine, and foie gras. Its location in the Old Quarter is also an advantage for those looking to pair dinner with exploring central Hanoi. Address: 12 Lo Su Street, Hoan Kiem Ward. Prices are around VND500,000 per person, not including alcoholic drinks. Samé - bistrot & wine Samé follows a French bistro style with a Vietnamese touch, and has 30 covers. It uses Vietnamese ingredients, which sets it apart from other French restaurants in the city. Popular dishes include beef carpaccio, whole fried quail with smoked sriracha sauce, and light bites such as paprika fries. Address: 29 Le Thanh Tong Street, Cua Nam Ward. Prices are around VND500,000 per person, not including alcoholic drinks.

picked.t: Two Ho Chi Minh City students win iPhone 17s for frequent bus travel
picked.body: The awards were presented Friday by the Ho Chi Minh City Public Transport Management Center, based on data from its payment and identification system. The center identified 10 students with the highest number of valid bus trips between Oct. 1 and 15. Tran Thanh Luong, a student at the University of Transport in Ho Chi Minh City, topped the ranking and received an iPhone 17 with 256 GB of storage. The other nine students were selected through a lucky draw. Le Quy, a student at the College of Radio and Television II, won the second iPhone 17 256 GB, provided by another sponsor. The remaining students received shopping vouchers worth VND1-2 million each. "I’ve taken the bus about 200 to 300 times (over Oct. 1-15)," Luong said. He regularly travels by bus to university and his part-time job. He also uses the journeys to observe transport management and operations, the field he is studying. "I never imagined that riding the bus could lead to winning an iPhone," Quy said, adding that buses are a convenient way for students to get around. Le Hoan, deputy director of the center, said this was the first time it had organized such a program. The initiative aims to encourage students and young people to use public buses and help ease traffic congestion. The center plans to continue it. Ho Chi Minh City has offered free rides on 134 public bus routes since July 1. These routes have carried more than 40 million passengers since, nearly 50% more than during the same period last year.

picked.t: Vietnamese single mother raises two children through travel and self-study
picked.body: At 6 a.m. on an early November morning, inside a mobile home parked in Son Tra Ward in Da Nang, Thi urged her daughter, Nhu Y, 14, to log into her online sewing class. While her daughter was in class, she phoned her son, Duy Thanh, to ask about his life in the dormitory of Vietnamese-German University in HCMC. In early September, he was admitted to the university’s electrical and computer engineering program on the strength of a GED certificate (equivalent to a U.S. high school diploma), an IELTS score of 7.5, and an SAT score of 1,390. These results came from Thanh’s five years of self-study. The family's nomadic life began following a tragedy in 2020. At the time, the HCMC native was working as an accountant while her husband was a bus driver. He was diagnosed with cancer and passed away within two months. Having lost her income after taking time off to care for her husband, she moved back to her mother's house with her two children, selling yogurt at the local market and crocheting to make ends meet. After his father's passing, Thanh, then 12 years old, became addicted to video games. Meanwhile, the memory of her husband's cancer made Thi pay greater attention to their living environment and food sources. She began researching in online communities of people who had left the city for the countryside By 2021, Thi sold her house and land, and moved her two children from HCMC to a house borrowed from a friend in Cu M’gar Commune in the central Dak Lak Province. Living alongside the Ede ethnic minority people, she noticed local children often accompanied their parents to the fields in the morning and attended school in the afternoon, yet remained healthy, had strong immune systems, and were helpful to others. This observation prompted her to redesign her children's education. Taking advantage of the shift to online schooling during the Covid-19 pandemic, she enrolled her two children in homeschooling under the United States’ Acellus program, which cost US$25 per month. All subjects were taught in English. To tackle her son's gaming addiction, she handed him a hoe to till the soil and clear weeds. She involved both children in tasks such as painting and repairing abandoned houses and building cabinets. Every day, Thanh went out with friends to play in the rain and splash around in streams, and helped tend fields of okra, scallions, cilantro, and radishes. Thanks to the increased outdoor physical activity, he spent significantly less time on his computer. Each month, she took her children to agricultural workshops where they learned to saw bamboo to build trellises for sponge gourds, prepare soil for growing vegetables, and study clean agriculture models, how biomass stoves work, and how to recycle biochar byproducts. To earn an income, Thi sold farm produce online and referred guests to homestays. Their nomadic life began when the family started relocating every three to six months, moving through places such as Hue, Da Nang, Binh Dinh Province, and Tuy An Nam Commune in Dak Lak Province. In mid-2023, while renting a home near the coast of Tuy An Nam, she sent Thanh to help out at Phuoc Luu’s coffee shop in Lo Village to gain real-world experience. Over three months, he waited tables, looked after the dogs, tended the garden, and learned how to make drinks. Outside of work hours, Thanh went swimming in the ocean with local children and studied on his computer in the evening. When Luu opened a community bookstore next to the coffee shop, Thanh helped clean, set up the premises, and plant vegetables and flowers with the younger kids. His strong English skills allowed him to serve foreign customers. He also joined trekking, camping, and waterfall expeditions, helping carry gear, cook meals, take photos, and support others. "The boy completely changed after that summer, becoming proactive, lively, and outgoing," Luu says. To make moving easier, in early 2025, Thi purchased and renovated an old mobile home for VND800 million. The shower area was downsized to make room for a kitchen cabinet and a washing machine. Inside this vehicle, Nhu Y has a dedicated corner for sewing, embroidery, and playing the violin. Both her children are now in charge of their own study schedules. Thi only monitors the schedules and uses an app to track the total hours they study each day.. "There is no single best educational environment for everyone, only an environment that fits each child," Thi says about her family's five-year journey.

picked.t: Vietnam, Thailand draw growing interest from Czech holidaymakers
picked.body: According to travel company Student Agency, Hanoi has become one of the three most sought-after destinations among its customers this winter. Searches for flights to Hanoi have increased 47% year-on-year. Company spokesman Lukas Kubat said the trend could partly be driven by the launch of a new direct air route between Prague and Hanoi in October 2026. However, Bangkok and Phuket in Thailand remain the company's top-selling destinations. The Association of Tour Operators and Travel Agents of the Czech Republic (ACCKA) said popular long-haul destinations for the Christmas and New Year holidays include Thailand, Zanzibar, the Dominican Republic, the Maldives, Vietnam, the Philippines and Mexico. Among closer destinations, Egypt remains a popular choice. ACCKA Executive Director Katerina Chaloupkova said customers mainly favour all-inclusive holidays lasting around one week although some also plan longer trips, particularly to Egypt. Cambodia and China's Hainan Island are among the new destinations served by direct charter flights from Prague. Travel companies said the expansion of direct routes has made distant destinations more accessible to holidaymakers. Petr Kostka of Exim Tours said non-stop flights shorten travel times and make long-haul destinations more attractive to customers. Travel agency Fischer has reported a similar trend. Its spokesman Jan Bezdek said Vietnam, Cambodia, the Dominican Republic and Zanzibar are among the destinations favoured by its customers. Prague Airport's winter flight schedule this year connects the Czech capital with 145 destinations, 12 more than last year. In contrast to the growing popularity of destinations in Asia and other regions, Czech travel companies have reported year-on-year declines of tens of percentage points in visitor numbers to the United Arab Emirates (UAE) and Oman. Kostka said Exim Tours has yet to resume charter flights to the two countries. Regional conflicts are considered one of the factors weighing on travel demand. However, the decline in visitor numbers to some Middle Eastern countries does not indicate weaker demand among Czech travelers for long-haul holidays. Rather, customers are shifting towards alternative destinations.

picked.t: Rain triggers morning traffic jams in Hanoi
picked.body: From 7 a.m. onward, Tran Duy Hung Street experienced heavy congestion as a surge of vehicles headed into the city center amid the rain. Long lines of traffic moved at a crawl, making it difficult for commuters to reach work. According to the National Center for Hydro-Meteorological Forecasting, a cold air mass brought moderate to heavy rainfall, with some areas seeing thunderstorms. This weather system also caused a drop in temperatures across the capital city, bringing outdoor temperatures down to 20 degrees Celsius on Monday morning. Motorbikes and cars crammed the roadway between the Thanh Xuan underpass and the Nguyen Chi Thanh-Tran Duy Hung intersection. The Ring Road 2-Nguyen Trai intersection has been a notorious rush-hour bottleneck since it first opened. Traffic frequently backs up from the junction onto the Nguyen Trai overpass and at two key U-turn points, triggering a multi-directional gridlock that brings movement to a near standstill.

picked.t: South Korean low-cost airlines slash Southeast Asia fares as tourists favor Japan, China
picked.body: Jeju Air is offering discounts of up to 77% on February flights from Incheon and Busan to Vietnam, Thailand, Malaysia, and the Philippines, ChosunBiz reported. Trinity Airways, formerly T'way Air, is cutting Southeast Asian fares by 22% for travel through January. A Jeju Air flight from Incheon to Da Nang on Nov. 21 has base fares starting at just 10,000 won, while Trinity Airways listed an Incheon-Nha Trang flight on Nov. 1 for 15,000 won. However, fuel surcharges and airport fees can add 110,000-190,000 won each way, with extra baggage and meals potentially costing further. Airlines are lowering fares to fill seats on flights they need to maintain to retain operating rights and airport slots. Selling cheap tickets helps cover some costs, even if the flights remain unprofitable, industry officials told ChosunBiz . Routes between Incheon and Vietnam carried 7.33 million passengers in the first nine months of the year, down 5.4% from a year earlier, according to Air Transportation Information Portal data. Passenger numbers on the Thailand and Philippines routes fell by 14% each. On the other hand, passenger traffic between South Korea and Japan rose by 20.3% in the first eight months, while China routes recorded a 23% increase, Seoul Economic Daily reported, citing transport ministry data. The newspaper said a weak yen had helped attract travelers to Japan, and new flight connections had made China more accessible. Shorter flights also mean lower fuel surcharges than trips to Southeast Asia. Alongside fare cuts, Trinity Airways plans to suspend certain flights to Da Nang, Nha Trang, and Bangkok during the winter schedule to limit losses.

picked.t: 베트남 부총리 “친환경 모빌리티 전환, 강제해선 안 돼”…자발적 전환 장려 촉구
picked.body: 호치민시의 한 거리에서 퇴근길 오토바이들이 신호 대기 중인 모습.  베트남 대도시를 중심으로 친환경 모빌리티 전환이 가속화되고 있는 가운데 정부는 시민들로 하여금 전기차 전환을 강제해서는 안 된다는 방침을 밝혔다. 베트남 정부사무국은 팜 지아 뚝(Pham Gia Tuc) 상임부총리의 이러한 지시사항을 담은 지침을 지난 5일 공포했다. 뚝 부총리는 이번 지침을 통해 사회경제적 여건과 교통 인프라 실정에 맞춰 국민과 기업이 스스로 친환경 교통수단으로 옮기도록 장려하는 해법 마련을 건설부에 지시했다. 뚝 부총리는 관련 정책에 차량 소유자와 국민, 기업이 순수 전기차나 친환경 교통수단으로 바꿔야 한다는 의무 규정이나 의무 로드맵이 포함되어서는 안 된다는 점을 강조했다. 베트남 수도 하노이와 남부 최대 도시인 호치민시는 그동안 친환경 모빌리티 전환 로드맵 아래 저배출구역(LEZ) 시범 운영 등 오염물질 배출이 많은 내연기관 차량에 대한 규제를 지속적으로 확대하는 움직임을 보여왔다. 실제로 하노이는 지난 7월부터 호안끼엠동(phuong Hoan Kiem) 내 2곳에서 LEZ를 시범 운영하고 있다. 해당 지역에서는 내연기관 이륜차 통행이 제한되지는 않으나, 영업용 이륜차를 중심으로 운행 제한이 권고되고 있다. 자가용의 경우, 시당국은 2008년 이전 생산·수입된 이륜차와 2016년 이전 출고된 이륜차의 사용 제한을 권장하고 있으며, 지역민들로 하여금 친환경 차량 전환이나 대중교통 사용을 장려하고 있다. 호치민시 역시 친환경 모빌리티 전환 로드맵을 통해 LEZ 지정안을 검토하고 있다. 현재 마련된 초안에 따르면, 오는 2028년 1월부터 2029년까지는 도심지와 투티엠(Thu Thiem) 신도시 지역이 LEZ로 지정될 예정이며, 2030년부터는 제2순환도로 내부로 LEZ 범위가 확대될 예정이다. 또한 호치민시는 2027년부터 관내 모든 시내버스를 친환경 버스로 전환할 계획이다. 정부기관 또는 공공기관 역시 자동차와 이륜차 등 관용차를 새로 구입하거나 교체 시기가 도래한 경우, 이 요건을 충족해야 한다. 나아가 호치민시는 2030년부터 택시 및 영업용 이륜차의 친환경 전환을 의무화하고, 2045년까지 관내 모든 차량을 친환경 차량으로 전환한다는 목표다.

picked.t: 베트남, ‘중국·인니·대만’ 수입산 스테인리스강 반덤핑조사 착수…9개 품목 대상
picked.body: 기사 이해를 돕기위해 AI를 활용해 제작한 이미지입니다. 베트남이 중국과 인도네시아, 대만에서 수입되는 일부 냉연 스테인리스강 제품에 대한 반덤핑 조사에 착수했다. 베트남 공상부는 지난 6일 중국과 인도네시아, 대만 등 3개국·지역에서 수입 중인 일부 냉연 스테인리스강 제품에 대한 반덤핑 조사 개시에 대한 결정문 제2948/QD-BCT호를 공포하고, 조사에 착수했다. 이번 조사는 베트남 제조 업계를 대표하는 포스코VST(Posco VST Co., Ltd)와 떤비엣금속과학기술(Tan Viet Metal Science and Technology Co., Ltd) 2곳의 청원에 따라 시작됐다. 이들 업체는 청원서를 통해 중국의 덤핑 마진을 76.6%, 인도네시아와 대만은 각각 75.5%, 51%로 제시했다. 조사 대상 품목은 두께 3.5㎜ 이하의 코일·시트·스트립 형태 냉연 스테인리스강으로, 열처리 또는 산세나 표면 스케일 제거 등 불순물을 없애는 가공을 거쳤는지는 따지지 않는다. HS코드는 7219.32.00, 7219.33.00, 7219.34.00, 7219.35.00, 7219.90.00, 7220.20.10, 7220.20.90, 7220.90.10, 7220.90.90 등 9개 품목이 조사 대상이다. 덤핑 여부를 판단하기 위한 조사 기간은 2025년 10월 1일부터 2026년 9월 30일까지이며, 국내 산업의 피해를 평가하는 기간은 2022년 10월 1일부터 2026년 9월 30일까지다. 공상부는 반덤핑 조사가 개시됨에 따라 관련 당사자에게서 정보를 수집한 뒤, 이를 바탕으로 해당 시장 수출업체의 덤핑 여부와 베트남 국내 산업의 피해 수준, 덤핑 혐의와 피해 사이의 인과관계를 평가할 예정이다. 조사 당국은 예비 조사 결과를 토대로 필요하다고 판단하면 공상부 장관에게 잠정 반덤핑관세 부과를 건의할 수 있다. 공상부는 조사 대상 제품을 수입, 수출, 유통, 거래하거나 사용하는 단체 및 개인에게 정당한 권익을 지키기 위해 이해관계자로 등록하고 필요한 정보 제공을 당부했다.
